correctness.rationale: For 2+1 bundles EFX is equivalent to the singleton owner receiving a maximum-valued good. The algorithm is a valid causal decision tree: first recipient fair coin; second decision based on revealed comparison; third determines feasible EFX completion. Case analysis for opposite first-two preferences and both possible same-preference orientations yields ≥1/2 for every real nonnegative additive valuation, including ties via canonical ranking. Two fixed positive identical-valuation inputs with equal first-two goods force disjoint split/pair events at time two, proving all algorithms have some input with success ≤1/2. Packaged verifier directly rechecks 15,625 profiles and both witness events. No finite experiment substitutes for the universal proof.

value.rationale: The 2026 motivating paper quantifies a gap between 1/3 and 1/2 already at the first nontrivial horizon of two agents and three goods; this exact tight randomized minimax probability closes the gap. The result separates adaptivity at the second arrival from advance lottery over entire recipient sequences and yields a transparent optimal online strategy. The information-limited 3-good model is natural, not an arbitrary parameter selection, because with ≤2 goods giving them to distinct agents guarantees EFX. Larger n and larger horizons remain open for this argument.
